title: Historical result lookup and selected execution repairs

changes.behavior: If an execution-scoped result URI mapping is missing, recover only a cache entry for the exact producing execution and output port. Reject a mismatched producer or port. Existing historical mappings take precedence.

Execute accepts a nonempty unique operator_ids list. Run and materialize these operators and all upstream dependencies; retain other branches in the persistent graph. Validate only the selected closure. Reject unknown or disabled targets before execution. Omitted selection retains whole-graph execution.

Document selected execution for current task outputs and historical forks. Preserve retrieve freshness rules, ordered actions, and the boundary between receiving an observation and deciding the next action.

regressions_before.bun: 4 failures reproduced across the new selected-action and execution validation tests.
regressions_before.scala: Exact cached producer lookup after registry cleanup failed; mismatched producer rejection passed.

validation.native_references: regenerated and verified by the tests
validation.manual_live_trace_audit: An intentional Process failure is reported. A later selected execution computes current total 357 and the rewired historical-formula total 157, excluding the failed sibling and incomplete consumer. Historical task-1 total remains 15. Both excluded operators remain in the graph. Whole-graph execution rejects the incomplete input.

limitations: This is deterministic implementation verification; LongDS accuracy and cost improvements have not been measured for this new candidate.
Selected execution must name the current outputs. Whole-graph execution still includes every branch. A failing dependency inside the selected closure still fails that execution.
Historical lookup recovery requires retained cache metadata and the materialized result document. It does not restore evicted or physically deleted data.
Statistics-persistence concurrency remains outside this two-fix change.
The local CSV engine smoke did not require file-service or frontend. The private file-service startup failed during setup and was skipped; no shared services were targeted.
